references.text: Earlier verses in the same chapter dealing with responsibility for another's property and compensation for damage or loss
Continuation of the law regarding the keeping of animals, describing an oath to the Lord and liability for restitution
Jacob describes his responsibility as a shepherd for Laban, where he had to replace animals that were torn apart or stolen
Legislation concerning faithlessness toward the Lord regarding entrusted goods, deposits, or property robbed from one's neighbor
Provisions concerning confession of sin and restitution when one has acted treacherously against one's neighbor
Ezekiel speaks about the shepherds of Israel and their responsibility to watch over the flock
Complementary laws regarding animal loss: 22:9 covers loss without witnesses (liability), while 22:3 covers theft with capture (punishment).
Parallel on liability for damage to another's animals: 21:33 (negligence regarding a pit) and 22:9 (responsibility as a keeper).
Complementary ethical principles: 22:9 (liability as a keeper) and 22:4 (general duty to help another's animal).
Complementary rules concerning wild animals: 22:9 (liability for loss during storage) and 23:4 (duty to return).
